frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Cultivation-for-yield: the deliberate working of a substrate (ground, and by extension any domain treated as ground) so as to bring forth produce/return — i.e., tillage as a productive enterprise, present either as the act of tilling/sowing (verb) or as the tilled field / its cultivated yield-locus (noun).

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Cultivation-for-yield: the deliberate working of a substrate (ground, and by extension any domain treated as ground) so as to bring forth produce/return — i.e., tillage as a productive enterprise, present either as the act of tilling/sowing (verb) or as the tilled field / its cultivated yield-locus (noun).
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 14 occurrences the root names not "crop" as a finished thing, nor "land" as bare ground, but WORKED, YIELD-DIRECTED cultivation. The single verb form makes the act explicit: "Have you seen that which you till/sow (taHruthūna)?" (56:63) — an act of human labor on soil aimed at produce. The literal noun cluster names the tilled field or its cultivated crop as the object/site of that labor: David and Solomon judging over al-Harth into which sheep strayed at night (21:78) — a standing tilled field; the corrupter who "destroys the Harth and the offspring/nasl" (2:205) — cultivation paired with breeding as the two engines of yield; the cow "that does not water/irrigate the Harth" (2:71) — Harth as the irrigated worked field; wind that strikes and destroys "the Harth of a people" (3:117) — the crop-in-cultivation; Harth listed among worldly acquisitions beside cattle (3:14, 6:136, 6:138) — the cultivated holding; "go early to your Harth if you would reap/be harvesters (ṣārimīn)" (68:22) — the field approached precisely for its return. The two metaphorical clusters keep the very same cultivate-for-yield frame and only swap what is cultivated: "Your women are a Harth for you, so come to your Harth as you wish, and send ahead for yourselves" (2:223 ×2) — women figured as the field one tends for offspring, with the forward "send ahead for yourselves" preserving the yield/return vector; and "Whoever desires the Harth of the Hereafter, We increase him in his Harth; whoever desires the Harth of the world, We give him of it" (42:20 ×3) — one's strivings figured as cultivation whose produce is the reward, "We increase him in his Harth" being explicitly the augmenting of a return. Subtracting form (I verb vs. verbal-substantive noun), construction (fī l-Harth locative, iḍāfa harth-hu/harth-kum possessive, harth al-ākhirah genitive-of-domain), participants (David/Solomon, spouses, strivers, wrongdoers), and register (legal, marital, eschatological, polemical) leaves in every case the same residue: substrate worked for produce/return.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: the lone verb (56:63 taHruthūna) supplies the ACT reading (tilling/sowing); the 13 nouns supply the RESULT/LOCUS reading (tilled field or its cultivated yield). Both reduce to the same cultivation-for-yield residue — verbal vs. nominal packaging, not a difference in root content. CONSTRUCTION: locative fī l-Harth (21:78, 2:71) foregrounds Harth as a place because "into/in" needs a site; possessive harthaka/harthihi (2:223, 42:20, 68:22) foregrounds it as an owned productive holding; genitive harth al-ākhirah/al-dunyā (42:20) supplies the DOMAIN in which cultivation is imagined — none of these vectors is contributed by the root, they are added by the frame. PARTICIPANTS/CONTEXT: the marital (2:223) and eschatological (42:20) metaphors, the legal grazing-damage case (21:78), and the polemic over dedicating produce to idols (6:136, 6:138) determine WHAT is cultivated and to what end, but the cultivation-for-yield core is invariant beneath all of them.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 2:223 ("Your women are a Harth for you; so come to your Harth as you wish"). It is the hardest because the referent is a person, not soil, so a naive "field/land" gloss fails. It reconciles cleanly under the abstract residue: the woman is figured as the cultivable field the spouse tends, and the yield vector is made explicit in the same breath — "wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum" (send/put forward for yourselves), i.e. cultivate now for a return (offspring). The metaphor operates on the OBJECT of cultivation, not on the root's meaning, which remains "worked substrate directed at produce." A close second is 42:20's "Harth of the Hereafter," equally reconciled by "nazid lahu fī harthihi" — the promise to INCREASE the return names the cultivate-for-yield core outright.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is "crop / produce" (the harvested growing-thing itself) as the core. It covers the destruction verses well (2:205, 3:117 — a crop is what is destroyed) and the acquisition lists (3:14, 6:136). But internal evidence arbitrates against it: (1) the verb 56:63 taHruthūna denotes the ACT of tilling/sowing, not a produced crop, and its own context contrasts human tilling with God's causing-to-grow — so the root sits on the labor/cultivation side, not the finished-produce side; (2) 2:71 "does not water the Harth" and 68:22 "go early to your Harth to reap" treat Harth as the worked field one irrigates and approaches for harvest, not as the harvest; (3) 2:223 figures a person as Harth — intelligible as a field/cultivation-site, incoherent as "a crop." A second alternative, "land/field" alone, fails symmetrically because it cannot host the verb (an act) or the "increase in his Harth" return-language (42:20). "Cultivation-for-yield" is the only center that spans act, locus, and yield-domain.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors are zaraʿa/zarʿ (ز ر ع, the sprouting/growing crop and its growth, which the Qur'an assigns to divine causation), nabata/nabt (ن ب ت, spontaneous or caused sprouting of vegetation), and ghars/badhr (planting/seed-scattering). Hrv is distinct in foregrounding the HUMAN productive labor on a substrate for a return — tilling/sowing/tending a field one owns and reaps — rather than the vegetative growth itself. This distinction is internally attested at 56:63–64's frame, where "that which you till (taHruthūna)" is the human contribution set against the growing-power that is not theirs; Hrv is the working, zarʿ-type growth is the outcome. Falsifiability: if any occurrence applied Hrv to wild, unworked, or spontaneously-arising vegetation, or used it with no owner/labor/return element (pure ground, pure standing plant), the cultivation-for-yield residue would break. No occurrence does; every one carries a worker, a tended holding, or an explicit return.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — cultivation-for-yield (working a substrate to bring forth produce/return) — is recoverable in every one of the 14 occurrences after subtracting form, construction, participants, and context, and it survives the hardest cases: the verb (act of tilling, 56:63), the irrigation/harvest field-uses (2:71, 68:22), the destruction verses (2:205, 3:117), the acquisition lists (3:14, 6:136, 6:138), and the grazing-damage legal case (21:78). It is not forced onto them because they are the literal home of the sense. The direction is determinate (labor-toward-produce, distinct from divine growth-causing zarʿ, per 56:63–64) and the root is sharply distinguishable from its neighbors, which would argue STRONG. I hold it to MODERATE rather than STRONG solely because 5 of the 14 (2:223 ×2 women-as-field; 42:20 ×3 Harth-of-Hereafter/world) are metaphorical extensions requiring an inference step — though that step is unusually well anchored: each metaphor retains the cultivate-for-yield frame ON ITS SURFACE via explicit return-language ("send ahead for yourselves," "We increase him in his Harth"), so the extension is internally bridged and none goes unreconciled. No occurrence lands in inconsistent_refs; presence is clean across all 14.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 14 occurrences found no genuine failing case. Literal cluster (21:78, 2:71, 3:117, 2:205, 68:22, 56:63) is a textbook fit: tilled field / act of tilling-sowing, yield-directed. Hardest cases were the possession-listing triple (3:14, 6:136, 6:138) where Harth sits among wealth beside cattle/gold — I pressed whether this is "finished crop as commodity," which the candidate explicitly excludes. It survives: Arabic Harth denotes tilth / standing cultivated field-and-crop, not detached stored grain (which would be a distinct lexeme), so even as a possessed asset it names the cultivation-locus, not a finished detached product. Metaphorical clusters (2:223 women-as-field ×2; 42:20 hereafter/world strivings ×3) are principled extensions that retain the cultivate-for-yield frame and merely swap the substrate — "send ahead for yourselves" and "We increase him in his Harth" preserve the produce/return vector, so this is not ad-hoc rescue or over-breadth. Distinctiveness is strong and, notably, self-reinforced by the text: 56:63's continuation opposes Harth (human tilling/sowing) to zar' (God's causing-to-grow: "a-antum tazra'ūnahu am naHnu al-zāri'ūn"), giving a lexical boundary against the nearest neighbor zr'; further discriminated from Hsd (reap/harvest — cf. 68:22 where Sārimīn/reaping is a SEPARATE act applied TO the Harth), nbt, and ghrs. Failure condition (Harth meaning bare unworked ground, harvested grain-as-food, or an unrelated sense) is clear and unmet. Verdict SUPPORTED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: fī l-Harth into which sheep strayed at night (nafashat fīhi ghanam): a standing tilled field — the worked yield-locus damaged by grazing. Residue present.
yuhliku al-Harth wa-l-nasl: cultivation paired with breeding as the twin engines of yield the corrupter destroys — the cultivated substrate exactly.
nisā'ukum Harth lakum: metaphor bridged by candidate's own logic — women figured as the field tended for offspring; the qaddimū (send ahead) preserves the yield/return vector.
fa'tū Harthakum: same field-metaphor, imperative to approach the cultivated substrate; produce/return frame retained via 'send ahead for yourselves'.
lā tasqī al-Harth: cow that does not irrigate the field — Harth as the irrigated worked field, the productive-cultivation substrate itself.
aṣābat Harth qawm... fa-ahlakat-hu: the crop-in-cultivation of a people struck and destroyed by cold wind — worked yield-locus. Residue present.
al-Harth listed among worldly matāʿ beside cattle/gold: the cultivated holding as an object of acquisition — yield-producing substrate.
nazid lahu fī Harthihi: metaphor bridged by candidate logic — striving figured as cultivation; 'We increase him in his Harth' is explicitly the augmenting of a return/yield.
Harth al-ākhirah: one's eschatological strivings as cultivation whose produce is the reward — cultivate-for-yield frame, domain-as-ground extension.
Harth al-dunyā: worldly striving figured as cultivation yielding worldly return; same frame, swapped only in what is cultivated.
mā taHruthūna: the sole verb — 'that which you till/sow', explicit act of human labor on soil aimed at produce. Core residue.
ighdū ʿalā Harthikum in kuntum ṣārimīn: go early to your field if you would reap — field approached precisely for its harvest/return.
mimmā dhara'a mina l-Harth wa-l-anʿām: cultivated produce paired with cattle as God's created yield-sources apportioned by the polytheists.
anʿām wa-Harth ḥijr: cultivated holding paired with cattle, declared taboo — the yield-producing substrate as property. Residue present.
